chunks: 5 - Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr, from Hisham b. al-Hakam. He said:

Abu Shakir al-Disani visited Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq (upon him be peace). He said to him: Indeed you are one of the shining stars, and your forefathers were brilliant full moons, your foremothers were great intellectuals (4), your origin is the most noble of origins, and when scholars are mentioned, then fingers are folded counting you first. So inform me, O riffling overflowing ocean, what is the proof of the creation of the world? Al-Sadiq (upon him be peace) said: It is proven by the nearest of things. He said: And what is it? He said: Al-Sadiq (upon him be peace) called for an egg and placed it on his palm. Then he said: This is a well-protected fortress. Inside it is a thin membrane (1), surrounded by liquid silver and liquid gold. Then it splits open in the form of a peacock. Did anything enter it? He said: No. He said: So this is the proof of the creation of the world. He said: You have informed succinctly, and you have spoken beautifully. And I have known that we do not accept except what we comprehend with our eyes, or hear with our ears, or feel with our hands, or smell with our noses, or taste with our mouths, or what is imagined in the hearts as perception, and what the intellect deduces with certainty. So al-Sadiq (upon him be peace) said: You mentioned the five senses, and they do not benefit anything without a proof, just as darkness is not cut off without a lamp (2).

key_terms.الحواس الخمس: the five senses — sight, hearing, touch, smell, taste
key_terms.حدث العالم: the creation of the world — the theological argument that the world came into being
key_terms.حصن ملموم: well-sealed fortress — metaphor for the egg's shell
key_terms.دليل: proof/evidence — rational demonstration for the existence of God
key_terms.مصباح: lamp — metaphor for rational proof that guides the senses

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq use an egg to prove the existence of God to Abu Shakir al-Disani?
ai.summary: Hisham b. al-Hakam narrates that Abu Shakir al-Disani, a known skeptic, visited Imam al-Sadiq (as) and after praising him eloquently, asked for proof that the world was created. The Imam called for an egg and explained it as a sealed fortress containing a thin membrane with liquid silver (egg white) and liquid gold (yolk), which then splits open to produce a creature like a peacock -- all without anything entering it from outside. This proves a Creator. Abu Shakir acknowledged the beauty of the proof but insisted he only accepts evidence from the five senses. The Imam replied that the senses are useless without rational proof, just as darkness cannot be cut through without a lamp.
